name: correctness

findings.message: The `iter > 0` guard is always true because `iter` starts at 1, so `stage.start` is now unconditionally emitted for every cycle member in every run—fresh and resumed—violating GUAR-1 (a fresh run must behave exactly as today); before this change cycle members never emitted `stage.start`, and the design doc (Gap 7) explicitly named this guard wrong.

The CMBR-1 skip guard is never activated when a run is interrupted during iter=1: `_persisted_iter` is 0 (the init value, since `_cycle_state_write_iter_atomic` writes `current_iter=N` only at the END of each iteration), so `_start_iter=1` and the `_start_iter > 1` condition is false; already-complete iter-1 members (e.g. 'build') are re-dispatched on resume instead of being skipped.

When CMBR-1 skips a complete member it issues a bare `continue` without adding that member's persisted verdict and status to `blob`; the predicate blob for the resumed iteration is therefore missing that member's entry, so any `exit_when`, `abort_when`, or `until` predicate that references the skipped member evaluates against an absent key and can neither converge nor abort correctly.

The ITER-1 fixture writes `current_iter=2` by running 2 full rounds via `zb_engine_loop_state`, but in a real run interrupted during iter=2 `current_iter` would be 1 (written at the end of iter=1); the test therefore validates a state shape that never arises naturally, masking the fact that real interrupted-in-iter-2 state causes `_start_iter=1` and re-runs iter=1.
